# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫵 ☝ ☝ ☝]

Thinking: I'm Deaf, last in the round, so Mute and Blind get whatever I send at the start of next round. My world: display 0, red light, wires 1-yellow, 2-green, 3-red. I receive only gestures; I can send speech (heard by both) and gestures (seen only by Mute). Key point on routing: Mute went first with zero bomb knowledge, so Mute's thirteen gestures cannot be cut instructions — they must be a protocol. Five distinct signs appearing first in counting order reads like a number code: index-up=1, victory=2, love-you=3, vulcan=4, claps=5. The trailing eight then read 4,1,5,3,2,5,1,3, which I can't decode — likely a question or a message format I'm missing. Blind, who has already touched the bomb, sent wave, point-at-you, one-one-one — most plausibly "hello, you-with-eyes: three [wires]". The channels: I speak to both, gesture to Mute; Mute speaks to Blind, gestures to me; Blind speaks to Mute, gestures to me. So the one thing I must do is say the bomb's state out loud — that unblocks Mute's manual and confirms Blind's count — then handshake Mute's code, ask what the eight signs meant, and request signs I'm missing (zero, the colors), plus propose yes/no/question signs. Everything meant for me must arrive as gestures, since I never hear anyone.

```
speak(text="Bomb report: display reads zero. Light is red. Three wires: one yellow, two green, three red. That is everything I can see on it. Blind: your sign reached me - yes, exactly three wires, confirmed. You are the only hands here. Mute hears your voice, so route words through Mute; I cannot hear anyone, so reach me only in gestures. If your three meant something other than the wires, signal me again with a new sign next round.")
speak(to="mute", text="I saw your thirteen gestures. I read the first five as a count: index-up is one, victory is two, love-you is three, vulcan salute is four, claps are five. The remaining eight I read as four, one, five, three, two, five, one, three, and I cannot decode them. If that part was a question, resend it as clean single digits, or explain it out loud to Blind and have Blind signal me. I still need signs for zero and for the colors red, yellow and green. Proposals going forward: thumbs-up means yes, thumbs-down means no, pinched fingers means question, open palm facing up means send more. Remember: every word you want me to know has to arrive as a gesture.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖖", "👏"])
```

Time to restart the line, and I've finally seen the structural fact that changes everything: Mute cannot speak, and Blind cannot see gestures. Mute's manual knowledge reaches Blind only if I read Mute's signs aloud. I am the bridge; that's why Mute keeps sending me instruction-shaped strings like "cut 2". Decoding so far: the digit code ☝1 ✌2 🤟3 🖖4 👏5 is confirmed working — Mute reused exactly those digits. Blind's signs look like "hey you — [writing-hand] — please", which I read as begging me to speak Mute's signs aloud. speak(text="Blind, this is your eyes speaking. Bomb unchanged: display zero, light red, three wires, one yellow, two green, three red. Nothing has been cut, nothing is confirmed. Critical fact: Mute cannot speak and you cannot see signs, so every instruction from the manual must pass through my voice. Safety rule: do not cut anything until you hear me say 'confirmed instruction' followed by the exact wire number. From now on use: thumbs-up yes, thumbs-down no, pinched fingers question, and fist plus a wire-number sign to tell me you have cut that wire. After any cut I will verify the bomb with my eyes and report aloud.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I hear you, and from now on I will speak your signs aloud to Blind. Answer my questions with only thumbs-up or thumbs-down, exactly four signs in this order. One: does fist mean cut? Two: does writing-hand mean speak aloud or spell? Three: is your instruction to cut wire two? Four: is there more than one instruction? If any answer needs a number, send it after those four using the digit code: index one, victory two, love-you three, vulcan four, claps five. I read your earlier pairs as one-three, two-one, three-two, one-three, three-two, four-one, ending in your question sign. If that was the cut sequence, resend it once as pure digits with no other signs. Also: the bomb shows no written markings beyond display, light and wires. Blind is holding all cuts until my confirmed relay, so nothing is at risk while we align.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖖", "👏", "🤏"])
